messages:
anya: FYI perf alert from the canary that rolled kernel-affinity:v3. Host preproc CPU increased ~15% on ingress proxies. baseline window vs canary: CPU 62% -> 77%.

ben: saw it. flamegraph points to two hotspots: `ingress_proto::parse_headers` and `stream_writer::small_write_path`. lots of 40-200 byte writes.

lee: I pulled pprof + strace on a canary pod. syscall pattern: `write` count up 3x, `writev` almost zero. also see more frequent `kv_client::fetch` calls with lower reuse.

anya: kernel-affinity:v3 tries to bias toward minibatches if kernel_score delta < 0.03. intention was to shave 0.5ms on short sequences, but maybe we fragmented host batching.

ben: timeline: when canary receives burst of short seqs, selector assigns minibatch kernel, which completes faster on GPU -> host sends early partial frames back to proxy -> proxy flushes immediately (Nagle disabled) -> many tiny frames over http2 -> socket-level syscalls explode.

nina: ops-bot alerted about increased TX packets and higher per-pod interrupts. network team suggests adding application-level coalescing (buffer writes for up to 6ms) as a mitigation.

lee: ran a microbench: mix short=70%/long=30% with kernel-affinity:v3. baseline vs with coalesce=6ms: write syscall rate dropped 60%, kv hit-rate recovered from 88.9% -> 95.2%, overall host CPU delta reduced to +2%.

ben: nice. can you paste bench command and results summary?

lee: command: `./microbench --rps 800 --mix short:0.7,long:0.3 --dur 600 --tag kernel-affinity=v3 --host-flag coalesce_ms=6 --pprof on --ebpf-syscalls`
results: `write count 1.2M -> 480k, writev 3k -> 62k, kv_hits 88.9% -> 95.2%, cpu 77% -> 64%`

anya: action items: 1) rollback global rollout for 24h. 2) keep kernel-affinity baseline in repo but gate the delta (threshold) to prefer batching affinity when ingress short-seq density > 50%. 3) ship host coalescing toggle behind flag. 4) run end-to-end through our staging load generator for a full day.

ben: long-term: selector should account for host-side downstream effects (write amplification, kv residency) not just GPU latency. propose we add a selector-cost model with host-cost estimate derived from recent write/small-frame metrics.

nina: infra ask: can ops expose a per-proxy write-coalesce knob in runtime config so we can tune without deploy? ops-bot: creating ticket INFRA-5321.

anya: I'll open a short incident note and include flamegraphs + bench artifacts. lean toward delayed rollout until we have selector cost-model and ops coalescing. thanks everyone :slightly_smiling_face:

ops-bot: rollback: kernel-affinity:v3 -> kernel-affinity:v2 (initiated by anya).
